# SSH-008: No early drop-in shadows a later hardening setting

- **Group:** SSH
- **Severity when it fails:** moderate
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

sshd takes the first value it reads for most keywords, and drop-ins in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d are read in name order before the rest of the main file. A cloud-init file such as 50-cloud-init.conf with PasswordAuthentication yes beats a hardening file named 60-hardening.conf, which then does nothing while looking correct.

## Verify by hand

```sh
ls /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/; sudo grep -ri -E 'passwordauthentication|permitrootlogin' /etc/ssh/sshd_config /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/
```

## How to fix it

Rename the hardening drop-in to sort first (00-hardening.conf), or fix the earlier file, then confirm with sudo sshd -T.

Run `stackward explain SSH-008` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
